_comment: Release state per kernel and level (decision D14, judged in simulated cycles per sample since M13.1, D2708). On every level with a core model (`sse2`, `sse4.2`, `avx2`, `avx2-runtime`, `avx512`, `neon`) `cargo xtask check cycles` judges the committed results benches/results/cycles: `release` entries must stay within `_limits.release` times the cycles per sample of the comparison on both the reference model and the counter-model of the level, `dev` entries within `_limits.dev`; a ratio above `_limits.warn` and a `dev` entry within it (ready for `release`) are reported, and `_limits.goal` is reported per entry against a library only. At `simd128` (no core model) `cargo xtask count --platform wasm32` judges the instructions per sample the same way. `info` entries are reported and never judged; their `waiver` text says why the comparison is not fair. A `waiver` on a `release` or `dev` entry names the open item in docs/open-items.md that tracks a limit that is not met yet; it never hides the numbers. The level `avx2-runtime` is judged like every level against the reference library and needs its own entries (the maintainer's decision D2764): the gate takes the library's cycles and SNR from the `avx2` record of the entry (the same workload on the same models); an entry whose `avx2` comparison is our own fallback, or that is `info` at `avx2`, is `info` (D2765). The ratio of the run-time-detection build to our own fixed `avx2` build is information, never a status. D321 is a check, never a status; a `cycle_waiver` on a SIMD entry and level exempts it from that check (`cargo xtask check cycles`: the entry must not be slower than its `_fallback` entry on the reference model or the counter-model); its text gives the reason and names the open item in docs/open-items.md, and the check fails on a waiver whose gap is closed. Every entry was re-judged in cycles once with the full measurement of the CI measurement job (D2745, D2746): an entry over its cap went from `release` to `dev` only with an open item that names its numbers (I13.1-7, I13.1-8, I24-3; `avx2-runtime` re-judged against the library by D2765), never with a relaxed limit, and a `dev` entry within the release limit became `release`. Every judged record carries the SNR of ours and of the comparison against the f64 reference (`snr_db`, D2749): ours more than 1 dB below the comparison fails unless an `accuracy_waiver` gives the reason or the open item (D34). An `accuracy_trade` keeps a `release` entry above `_limits.release` at `release` while ours is at least 3 dB more accurate than the comparison, the comparison is below 100 dB (where accuracy is scarce; above it a few dB more have no practical effect) and ours is at most 1.20 times the comparison on both models (the maintainer's decision D2760: 3 dB better must not mean that we may be slow); its text names both SNR figures and the ratios. No status is ever decided by a comparison of our code with our own code (our fallback, our build of another level, our kernel): a `release` or `dev` entry whose judged comparison is not a library fails `cargo xtask check`, from the plan and from the `comparison_kind` of the records (D2767). A plain `waiver` keeps no `release` entry above `_limits.release` and a `dev` entry above `_limits.dev` only while it names its open item and says "awaiting the maintainer's decision" (D2779). See docs/performance.md.
